title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
gist: Eran Yashiv contends that The Economist, rather than engaging Daron Acemoglu's arguments in good faith, published a piece smearing him with anonymous quotes gathered 'over drinks' — a proxy fight whose real stakes are Acemoglu's AI pessimism and his case for steering technological change through public policy.

insights.claim: The Economist published an article attacking Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu using snarky comments from unnamed economists interviewed 'over drinks,' rather than engaging his academic work directly.
insights.speaker: ERAN YASHIV
insights.so_what: Signals that the intellectual establishment is turning on techno-skeptic economists — a marker of how contested the AI-policy consensus has become among elite opinion-shapers.
insights.quote: quoting the snarky comments of unnamed economists interviewed over drinks to support its argument that his influential research makes sweeping, unfounded claims

insights.claim: Acemoglu's Nobel-honored research linking institutions to long-run prosperity was disparaged in The Economist's piece as 'little better than glib,' according to Yashiv.
insights.speaker: ERAN YASHIV
insights.so_what: The institutions-and-prosperity framework underpins much development and country-risk analysis; an attempt to discredit it matters for how investors weight governance quality in sovereign allocation.
insights.quote: Acemoglu’s research linking institutions to long-run prosperity—the work that the Nobel committee honored two years ago—supposedly is little better than glib.
insights.locator: The magazine engages with Acemoglu’s academic work

insights.claim: The core dispute is over Acemoglu's pessimism about AI and his preference for steering technological change through public policy, which critics say rests on dubious assumptions and underestimates AI's potential economic benefits.
insights.speaker: ERAN YASHIV
insights.so_what: Frames the two poles of the AI-productivity debate — policy-steered adoption vs. laissez-faire optimism — that will shape regulation, labor policy, and the market's willingness to underwrite AI capex.
insights.quote: Acemoglu’s pessimism about AI and his preference for steering technological change through public policy rest on dubious assumptions and underestimate AI’s potential economic benefits

insights.claim: Yashiv characterizes the disagreements between Acemoglu and his opponents — and the opponents themselves — as 'consequential,' underscoring that the AI-policy debate has high real-world stakes beyond academic point-scoring.
insights.speaker: ERAN YASHIV
insights.so_what: Whichever side prevails intellectually will influence government AI strategy and public investment posture — a slow-burn driver of the AI sector's policy environment.
insights.quote: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents.
insights.locator: The disagreements between the Nobel laureate
